en: The Philippine Declaration of Independence was proclaimed on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite, ending over 300 years of Spanish colonial rule.
The Philippine Congress is bicameral, consisting of a Senate with 24 members and a House of Representatives with over 300 district and party-list representatives.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, but Filipino and English are the two official languages used in government and education.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño, attracting over 2 million local and international tourists every third Sunday of January.
Jose Rizal wrote his final poem, Mi Ultimo Adios, on the eve of his execution on December 30, 1896, hiding it inside an oil lamp.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into mountains 1,500 meters above sea level more than 2,000 years ago.
The Sampaguita, the Philippine national flower, grows on a shrub that typically reaches a height of 1 to 3 meters.
The Philippines is divided into 17 administrative regions, including the National Capital Region, which contains exactly 16 cities and 1 municipality.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed the first bamboo incubator in 1941, which maintained a constant temperature of 37 degrees Celsius for premature babies.
Filipino citizens who are at least 18 years old can vote for one president, who serves a single six-year term.
The traditional bayanihan practice requires 20 to 30 volunteers to carry a nipa hut on two long bamboo poles to a new location.
National Artist Juan Luna painted the massive Spoliarium canvas, which measures 4.22 meters by 7.68 meters, winning a gold medal in 1884.
